channel.title: RAN Air Wing dev blog
channel.description: HMAS Melbourne (R21) flight sim: history, carrier operations and dev diary.

item.title: Keyboard controls cheat sheet
item.description: Every key in the sim on one page: flight controls, cameras, and the commands for starting, stopping and restarting.

item.title: June 1947: Australia buys an unfinished carrier
item.description: How the RAN ended up with a half-built ship, a sister ship and a loan carrier.

item.title: Phase 2: a flyable A-4G Skyhawk
item.description: The ship got an aircraft: a Skyhawk with a simplified flight model, a cockpit view and a HUD, flown from the keyboard.

item.title: 28 February 1945: launched, then shelved
item.description: Launched months before the war ended, then left unfinished.

item.title: Wind over deck: why the ship turns into the wind
item.description: A carrier steams into the wind to give aircraft airflow over the deck. Here is the sum the sim does, and the numbers at each sea state.

item.title: 15 April 1943: the keel is laid at Barrow
item.description: A keel laid in wartime Barrow-in-Furness for a ship the Royal Navy would never commission.

item.title: How reference photos shaped the model
item.description: Twenty reference images, two drawings and a lot of squinting: how the ship's island, markings and deck layout were checked.

item.title: A carrier built to be thrown away
item.description: Australia's last conventional carrier began life as a wartime design that was never meant to last.

item.title: Pick your aircraft with a button
item.description: The menu now has a separate button for each flyable aircraft, the A-4G Skyhawk and the S-2 Tracker.

item.title: The loadout screen now shows the aircraft
item.description: A plan-view outline of the Skyhawk or Tracker on the loadout screen, with every pylon marked and clickable.

item.title: Simpler weapon selection and firing
item.description: The sim now remembers your weapon by name and switches for you when it runs dry, so K always fires what the HUD says.

item.title: Quick start: launch and land in five minutes
item.description: The fastest way to get a Skyhawk off the catapult and back on the deck, using the built-in tutorial.

item.title: Weapons now have sound: guns, rockets, bombs and torpedoes
item.description: Firing and releasing stores now makes noise, from the 20 mm cannon to a depth charge going off under the sea.

item.title: The jet blast deflector rises behind the Skyhawk
item.description: A hinged blast shield now lies flush in the deck behind the port catapult and rises when a Skyhawk reaches launch power.

item.title: Time skip: fast-forward the dull parts
item.description: A Time skip control in the menu speeds the whole sim up 2x, 4x or 8x, for transits and waiting.

item.title: Campaign missions: two Tracker sorties from the 1977 and 1980 cruises
item.description: The mission list gets a dated Campaign group: a search for a disabled merchant ship (1977) and a shadowing sortie (1980), both flown in the Tracker.

item.title: The LSO talks you down, and the meatball is on the mirror
item.description: The approach now has radio calls on screen, a 3D ball with datum and wave-off lights on the mirror, and an LSO grade for each trap.

item.title: Pedro: the plane guard Sea King gets its callsign
item.description: The rescue Sea King hovering off Melbourne's port quarter now carries a PEDRO tag, the nickname for the helicopter on station.

item.title: Flight hours, missions and aircraft choices, in public
item.description: The home page now shows what every pilot has logged, and a new Stats page breaks it down by aircraft and mission.

item.title: The A-4G's ailerons and rudder now move
item.description: The Skyhawk's ailerons and rudder are now separate surfaces that deflect with your stick and pedals, so you can see the controls working from the chase camera.
